A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UFM-based investigation of low-dimensional neural-network structure. Their complete main texts and appendices support comparison; rendered figures and tables resolve information missing from text extraction.

before.justification: V1 reports original gradient-descent simulations of linear and ReLU UFMs, including spectral and gradient-alignment measurements in Section 5 and Appendix G.

after.justification: V2 reports original UFM simulations and ResNet-20-based classification experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 in Section 5 and Appendix G.

M1.justification: The unconstrained-feature framework and linear/ReLU architectures remain. V2 specializes the MSE objective to uniform regularization, adds an analyzed CE-loss formulation in Appendix B, and changes the ReLU derivative convention from strict-positive gates to sigma'(0)=1. These are limited revisions of the analyzed models and derivative procedure.

E1.justification: V1's original experiments are confined to UFM simulations. V2 retains that coverage and adds actual handwritten-digit and natural-image classification experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10, substantially broadening empirical coverage beyond unconstrained synthetic features.

E2.justification: Neither version reports a competing-algorithm baseline comparison. Linear/ReLU UFMs and Papyan's decomposition remain subjects of theoretical validation; v2's added real-network experiments do not introduce competing comparison methods.

E3.justification: V1 uses K=3 and L=5, with linear d=60, l=3 and ReLU d=65, l=4. V2 uses K=4, L=4, d=65, l=3 for both. It adds ReLU parameter thresholding at 10^-6, changes the derivative convention, introduces orthogonality and effective-rank measurements, and adds real-network evaluation protocols in Appendix G.2.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of ReLU feature nonnegativity, orthogonal-frame convergence and a decaying rank-one perturbation, plus real-network singular-vector alignment and effective-rank analyses. Papyan knockout analyses are retained and extended. V1's gradient-covariance/backpropagation-error spectral experiments and ReLU row-orthogonality tables are removed rather than relocated.

E5.justification: V2 Figures 6, 16 and 18 introduce averages with one-standard-deviation error bars across class-indexed quantities or outlier values. Appendix G.2 identifies the displayed experiments as individual runs. V1 lacks comparable statistical summaries; the new bars do not establish repeated-run uncertainty or an increase in runs.

E6.justification: V1 Table 1 reports ReLU eigenvector alignments of 0.673 to 0.997 after one million epochs, while Table 2 reports unequal nonzero gradient components. V2 replaces these with trajectories approaching linear-model predictions under revised settings and derivative conventions. It also adds MNIST/CIFAR-10 spectral findings and MNIST effective ranks approaching 10 for weights and 100 for the Hessian. These are revised or new results, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Beyond retaining the layer-wise linear-UFM results, v2 adds full-Hessian results in Theorems 5–6, conditional ReLU extensions and an optimality characterization in Theorems 7–8, and CE spectral analysis in Theorem 9, with proofs in Appendices C, D and F. It also derives explicit spectral scales and weight singular vectors previously unspecified.

C1.justification: The unification thesis remains, but the abstract, introduction and conclusion expand the claimed contribution from principally layer-wise linear-UFM theory to ReLU theory, full-network Hessian structure and validation on actual image datasets. V2 additionally claims the first analytic account simultaneously reproducing all the cited low-dimensional spectral phenomena.

C2.justification: V1 leaves the missing mini-bulk and incomplete ReLU correspondence unresolved. V2 attributes the mini-bulk difference to MSE versus CE loss and explains ReLU behavior through nonnegative features and a slowly decaying rank-one perturbation. It adds substantive qualifications concerning ReLU DNC's nonglobal optimality, differentiability at zero, depth/regularization assumptions and the UFM's applicability to converged overparameterized networks.

D1.justification: V2 supplies explicit UFM regularization and numerical-threshold details and a substantial real-network recipe: ResNet-20 with four linear layers, feature/head regularization, MNIST subsampling, input standardization, batch size 10,000, and dataset-specific learning-rate schedules and training durations. V1 provides much sparser simulation settings, although its Gaussian-initialization disclosure is no longer stated in v2.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands research positioning through Appendix A's justification of UFMs and discussion of newer work on low-rank bias, DNC's nonglobal optimality and correspondence with real architectures. Added Sukenik and Garrod–Keating works directly shape the ReLU and CE analyses, while the introduction broadens connections to flatness, generalization and robustness.

P1.justification: The introduction, background and conclusion are extensively rewritten. V1's separate model exposition is consolidated into the background, its extended numerical narrative is condensed, and proofs are reorganized into model-specific appendices. Appendix A adds a substantial modeling rationale. This is extensive narrative restructuring beyond the scientific additions.

P2.justification: V2 removes the two UFM schematics and all four v1 tables, combines alignment measurements into multi-panel figures, and redesigns spectral displays. Weight spectra and knockout figures move into Appendix G, while new real-network plots include shaded variability bands. Figures are integrated throughout the shortened main exposition instead of largely clustering after the experimental text.

improvement.justification: V1's connection from linear UFMs to realistic networks relied heavily on analogy and inconclusive ReLU numerics. V2 substantially strengthens that argument through conditional ReLU/full-Hessian derivations, CE analysis addressing the missing mini-bulk, and documented MNIST/CIFAR-10 validation. Some earlier diagnostics disappear, and the broad claims remain limited by the special ReLU convention, UFM-style regularization and the backpropagation-spectrum mismatch acknowledged in Appendix E.2. Nevertheless, the new theoretical and empirical support materially improves the paper overall.
